newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss industry group says business remains slow.
newsitem.headline: Swiss industry group says business remains slow.

text.p: The Swiss trade and industry group SHIV sees few signs of an economic recovery, as capacity utilisation remains at low levels and production is slack.
In its latest report on the economy, SHIV forecast Swiss gross domestic product to fall by 0.3 to 0.5 percent in 1996.
The forecast is in line with those of economists and economic institutions which also expect negative growth this year and a modest pick-up in 1997.
"The economic picture of Switzerland at the end of the year offers hardly any bright spots," SHIV said in the report.
"The weakness in the economy which set in in the first quarter of 1995 has not yet been overcome," it added.

It said production was weak, and the building industry in particular was still stuck in a pervasive slump. Some parts of the export industry were showing signs of a revival. But the situation on the jobs market remained depressed, it said.

Improvements would depend to a large part on developments in important export markets, where some positive signs are beginning to show. But SHIV also said that in some countries such as Germany and France, a pick-up could be slowed by restrictive fiscal policy.
It saw some chance Swiss exports could improve in coming months, but added that the weakness in domestic consumption was likely to offset export gains.
It said households were likely to keep consumption moderate because of worries about the weak Swiss job market and other factors.
